scope: Observed public UX patterns inform original Neral routes and controls; no source visual design is copied.

sources.observed: Enterprise destination groups governance, permissions, audit logging and contact capture.
sources.adaptation: Security page explains evidence ownership, workspace roles, retention and review trail; no certification claims.

sources.observed: Task guidance makes scope and success criteria explicit before work begins.
sources.adaptation: Method page starts with criteria and case selection before comparison and evidence review.

sources.observed: A dedicated review workflow supports inspecting findings and returning to work requiring attention.
sources.adaptation: Neral review queue and case evidence retain owner, decision status and an explicit next action.

sources.observed: Team invitation is a distinct administration task.
sources.adaptation: Security page describes reviewer versus workspace-admin roles; public app screens keep reviewer ownership visible.

inference: Neral is a fictional model-evaluation product. Evaluation IDs, cases, controls and every sentence in the new designs are original scenario content, not features claimed for the referenced products.
inputImages: Only the four approved Neral V6 raster images are actual visual inputs. Public pages are text research, not attached visual references.

captureReview.observedVisually: Enterprise page separates product examples, governance, contact form and footer. Mobile collapses governance to ruled single-column rows. Review docs have persistent subject navigation and article-local navigation; categorized assigned review entry is explicit.
captureReview.adaptation: NERAL keeps its approved top navigation instead of adopting the source sidebar. Method and Security finish existing marketing navigation destinations, followed by evaluation, dataset and review workspace contexts.
